title: Shop won't replace or refund a defective product
triggers: shop refusing refund for defective phone
kharab saman wapas nahi le raha dukaandar

rights.plain_explanation: As a consumer you have the right to be heard and to seek redress against unfair trade practices.
Refusing to take back defective goods and refund you within the period on the bill, or within 30 days if none is stated, is an unfair trade practice.
You can file a complaint with the District Consumer Commission, including electronically.
You can file in the district where you live or work, not only where the seller is.
File within two years from when the problem arose.
The District Commission hears claims up to ₹50 lakh.

do_now: Keep the bill, warranty card and photos or videos of the defect.
Write to the seller or brand with a clear request (replace, repair or refund) and a deadline.
Call the National Consumer Helpline on 1915 to register a grievance.
user_at_fault_cases: Damage you caused, or claims outside the warranty period or terms, may not be covered.

escalation.label: National Consumer Helpline
escalation.detail: Call 1915 or register online before going to the commission.

escalation.label: District Consumer Commission
escalation.detail: File a complaint, online or in person, within two years.

escalation.label: Free legal aid
escalation.detail: Call NALSA on 15100 or visit your District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) at the district court. Women, children, people in custody and people below the income limit get a free lawyer.
